entities.summary:
Abdul Qadir Gilani (1166-02-21) was a prominent Hanbali scholar, preacher, and Sufi mystic leader whose influence reverberated across the Islamic world during the Medieval era. Born in unknown circumstances, Gilani's significance lies in his role as the founder of the Qadiriyya Sufi order, one of the oldest and most influential mystical traditions in Islam.

As a key figure in the intellectual landscape of his time, Gilani's teachings and writings had a profound impact on Islamic thought and culture. His emphasis on the importance of spiritual purification, moral rectitude, and the pursuit of knowledge helped shape the spiritual practices of millions of Muslims across the Middle East, North Africa, and beyond.

Gilani's legacy extends far beyond his own lifetime, influencing generations of Sufis, Islamic scholars, and spiritual seekers. His emphasis on the transformative power of love, compassion, and self-purification continues to inspire spiritual seekers and scholars to this day.

"The heart is the place of the soul, and the soul is the place of God." - Abdul Qadir Gilani
